claim: SEG maintains multi-node relationships linking claims to anchors and provenance.
Contradiction edges drive remediation workflows and audit visibility.
SEG graph schema defines 4 node types (Claim, Source, Derivation, Agent) and 5 edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, witnesses, cites).
SEG uses formal graph theory with bitemporal semantics: G = (V, E, τ_TT, τ_VT, θ, σ, ε).
SEG axioms include acyclicity (DAG for derivations), anchoring (every claim has source), temporal consistency, and contradiction resolution.
Edge weights reflect evidence strength: σ(supports) = authority(source) × relevance(source, claim).
Confidence propagation aggregates from supporting edges: confidence(claim) = Σ σ(supports_i) × confidence(source_i) / Σ σ(supports_i).
Graph traversal algorithms support impact analysis (reverse BFS) and lineage tracing (forward DFS).
SEG storage uses adjacency lists in CMC with indexes by tag, time, persona, and confidence.
Hyperedges enable multi-source evidence aggregation for claims supported by multiple anchors simultaneously.
Graph construction ensures consistency through axiom validation and bitemporal tracking.
Graph query operations enable efficient evidence retrieval and analysis through indexed lookups.
Contradiction detection uses semantic similarity and stance analysis to identify conflicting claims.
Graph performance characteristics enable real-time evidence analysis with sub-second query times.
Graph troubleshooting guide covers dangling claims, contradiction cascades, and temporal inconsistencies.
